top5.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites
top5.description: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to place a constellation of data centers in orbit. The authorization, valid for 15 years, allows the deployment of up to one million satellites.
top5.why: The FCC’s authorization for up to one million SpaceX satellites could reshape satellite communications, orbital computing and the competitive dynamics of space infrastructure.

top5.title: Nvidia suspends AI server shipments to four Asian countries
top5.description: Nvidia has asked its manufacturing partners to suspend AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The decision follows a new U.S. rule requiring licenses to export advanced chips to these countries.
top5.why: Nvidia’s suspension of AI-server shipments to four Asian countries shows how expanding U.S. export controls are disrupting the global AI hardware supply chain.

top5.title: Anthropic Shares Fall Below Their IPO Price
top5.description: Anthropic shares fell below their IPO price less than a week after going public, suggesting investors still doubt that revenue will exceed costs.
top5.why: Anthropic shares falling below their IPO price signals growing investor skepticism that frontier-AI revenues will justify the sector’s enormous computing costs.

top5.title: New York bans toys with AI chatbots for five years
top5.description: New York has become the second state, after California, to ban toys equipped with AI chatbots. The five-year ban will take effect 90 days after it is signed.
top5.why: New York’s five-year ban on AI chatbot toys marks a significant expansion of child-safety regulation that could influence product design and policy in other states.

top5.title: OpenAI tests private inference for businesses
top5.description: OpenAI’s Private Inference runs a company’s queries on its best models without OpenAI being able to see the data. The service is being tested with early business customers.
top5.why: OpenAI’s private-inference trial addresses a central barrier to enterprise AI adoption by promising businesses that their sensitive queries cannot be viewed by OpenAI.
